U.S. DISTILLATE stocks remain at the lowest for more than 40 years despite refiners running almost flat out to maximise production. Total stocks of diesel and other distillate fuel oils amounted to just 103 million barrels on October 23, the lowest for the time of year in weekly records stretching back to 1982. Inventories were 23 million barrels (-18% or -1.41 standard deviations) below the ten-year seasonal average and the deficit had narrowed only slightly from a peak of more than 30 million barrels (-22% or -1.67σ) in early September:

For the umpteenth time: The SoH is losing relevance. It’s the total exports out of the REGION that matter. Those wheels were set in motion once those who could, began diverting oil away from the SoH. Iraq now sends more via the Med and Saudi sends more via the Red. UAE increased pipeline usage.

Because when tankers are being fired upon, then you're going to prioritize what gets shipped out; and fetching $200M in crude oil revenue thanks to a large sturdy tanker makes a whole lot more sense than fetching $50M in diesel by a smaller tanker that risks sinking.

1) Pipelines are quick & easy to replace.
2) An excess of storage tanks is nice to have but not a deal-breaker.
3) Damaging a refinery only frees up more crude oil for exports. See Russia.
4) Stricken ships continue to the Gulf of Oman for STS and then get patched up.
